question: Why did America's ban on alcohol in the 1920s push drinkers from beer towards spirits?
answer: Because smuggling cost about the same per crate whatever was inside. A bootlegger risking a raid did better carrying whisky than bulky, cheap beer, so the illegal supply tilted to strong drink. Mark Thornton argued that the harder a ban is enforced, the more potent the product becomes. Speakeasies poured cocktails, not pints.
move: When moving something gets costly, expect the most concentrated version to win.
ask: When something I want gets harder to reach, do I start choosing its strongest form?
reference: Mark Thornton, Alcohol Prohibition Was a Failure, Cato Institute Policy Analysis No. 157, 1991
